page.layout: One page of running text, one column across the full measure. No margin notes. Running head at the top with the page number 142 at the left and the question mark "Q.XIV" at the right. Catchword "Lauren-" at the lower right.

main_text.p: nistrorum[?] & judicatura controversiarum; quæ sæpè oriuntur in Ecclesiâ ) integra manent sine impedimento secundùm verbum Dei illis, qui ad id officium in Ecclesiâ Christi vocati sunt, & id quidem sub suprema inspectione, curâ, autoritate & imperio Magistratus secundùm verbum Dei tàm in personas, quæ administrant cultum Dei, quàm in administrationem ipsam, ministros & alios, qui Ecclesiæ præsunt non debere quicquam amplius postulare, quandoquidem nec plus nec minus ipsis à Christo est mandatum. Ita Dominus Walæus; quemadmodum etiam ejusdem judicio omnes Orthodoxi Pastores gratias agere tenentur ei, qui asserit veram potestatem, quam Magistratus secundùm verbum Dei in negociis Religionis habet. Nam experientia omnium temporum, inquit, nos docet Ecclesiam tùm demum frui verâ suâ libertate, quando sub tali Magistratu est, qui intelligit & benè novit officium, quod Deus ei supra illam commisit, ait p. 9. editionis Gallicæ Amstelodamensis per H. Lauren-

page.notes: The first word of the first line is cut off at the left edge of the scan; it reads as "nistrorum", probably the end of "ministrorum". The line ends with "Lauren-" set right-aligned, which I have taken as the catchword. The "Q.XIV" in the right of the running head is a question number and is not part of the running title. Italic runs are judged from the scan and may not be exact at their edges.
